projects.title: Emergency Hospital Accessability Map
keywords: WebGIS, QGIS, Urban planning, Network analysis, Javascript, CSS, HTML, Leaflet
projects.description: An interactable web map of the accessibility to emergency hospitals in Stockholm County. The map is meant to create an overview of areas with weaker levels of access in the county, including population data to allow users to better understand & analyse how the population is impacted. The map has is based on a network analysis that uses road data from Trafikverket, a population grid from SCB, emergency hospital points from QuickOSM, and the county border from SCB. The project was a great way to reinforce the network analysis, and a fun way to explore webGIS with some programming languages and a commonly used library in Leaflet. There is a full documentation of the methods and data used available as a PDF.

projects.title: Wildfire Impact Analysis Interactive Map
keywords: WebGIS, ArcGIS Pro, Disaster Management, Copernicus, Vegetation Indexes, ArcPy Scripts, Javascript, CSS, HTML, OpenLayers, GeoServer, GDAL
projects.description:
This project is in the finishing stages, with some styling issues to work out, a couple of NDVI & NBR layers from later dates to be added. The website is currently available through the Github icon below the description, and is otherwise complete for the time being, but please feel free to share any thougths or questions!

It has been a very interesting project to accomplish, as it gave me much more hands-on experience working with rasters and satsatellite data. It has also been a great opertunity to get comfortable working with services and software such as the OpenLayers library, and the hosting service GeoServer, which was where the layers where first hosted as WMS & WFS. I could however not find a satisfactory way to serve the layers from GeoServer to the live version of the website, which led me to use GDAL for file optimization. It has been also been a significant step up in my understanding of JavaScript, HTML, and CSS.

The project has also utilized some very useful dependencies such as ol-ext for the swipe function, and chart.js for the charts. Getting familiar with how to download, manage, and use these dependencies has also given me a better understanding of tools like Vite, npm, and using the command line.
